Architectural overview

Problem & architectural thesis

Retail analytics and queuing models often lack clean, repeatable transaction datasets tied to physical floor layouts. PriceRiot pairs an ETL parameter extractor over historical POS CSVs with a C++17 discrete-event agent simulation core exposed cleanly to Python.

Control flow

  1. Propose / IngestPOS CSV ETL & YAML Store Spec

    Cleans raw POS transaction exports, maps SKUs, extracts arrival/basket parameters, and loads YAML store geometry.

  3. Deterministic CoreC++17 Engine + pybind11 Boundary

    Runs deterministic A* navmesh pathfinding for customer and worker agents across typed C++/Python bindings.

  5. Commit / AnalyzeSynthetic Transaction Logs & Dashboards

    Outputs structured transaction and queue logs to FastAPI/Vue 3 run comparison, Streamlit dashboards, and Jupyter notebooks.

Key tradeoff & failure mode

The simulation kernel, ETL ingestion pipeline, and analytics apps all run, but extracted parameters have not yet been calibrated or scored against held-out real store sales. Dynamic pricing hooks, queued-run worker updates (POST /api/runs/{id}/workers), layout optimization, and front-end tests remain unbuilt.

What it is

  • PriceRiot is a retail-store simulation: customer and worker agents pathfind (A* on a navmesh) through a YAML-defined store in a C++17 core exposed to Python through pybind11, and generate synthetic transaction records. #priceriot-engine
  • A POS ingestion pipeline cleans historical transaction CSVs, maps SKUs, and extracts simulation parameters, which the web app applies when a run has POS data attached. #priceriot-pos-etl
